title: Common submodule with coherent smaller-support cokernels
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $i:W\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $W$ integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], and let $\xi=i(\operatorname{genericPoint}W)$. Let $G$ be a coherent module [pqf-def-coherent] with $\operatorname{Supp}(G)=i(W)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], whose stalk at $\xi$ is killed by the ambient maximal ideal and is a one-dimensional module over $\kappa(\xi)$ [def-weil-residue-field], compatibly with the residue map. Let $I$ be a quasi-coherent ideal on $W$, represented by $W.\mathrm{IdealSheafData}$, and assume its pushforward [def-pc-module-pullback] $i_*I$ is nonzero. Then there exist a module $K$ and monomorphisms $a:K\to G$ and $d:K\to i_*I$ such that both canonical cokernels are coherent and finitely presented and each has nonzero-stalk support strictly contained in $i(W)$. No filtration is asserted.

proof.text: The closed subscheme W is Noetherian. Ideals on W are quasi-coherent finite type, hence coherent, and their closed pushforwards are coherent. If I were zero then its module and pushforward would be zero, contrary to the hypothesis.

Apply the generic-point ideal inclusion to G. The generic stalk is a residue-field line. The generic stalk of the source is a direct sum of copies of the generic ideal stalk, which is either zero or the generic field. Since the inclusion is an isomorphism near xi, that ideal J is nonzero and the number of summands is exactly one. Obtain an inclusion i_*J into G with invertible generic stalk.

Form L = I intersection J as IdealSheafData. On any nonempty affine open, nonzero elements from I and J have nonzero product in the integral domain, lying in L. Thus L is nonzero; all three generic stalk ideals equal the generic field. Set K = i_*L. Its inclusions into i_*I and i_*J, followed in the latter case by the inclusion into G, are monomorphisms. Coherent kernel/cokernel closure gives coherent cokernels. On a locally Noetherian scheme quasi-coherent finite-type modules are finitely presented, so both cokernels are finitely presented. Closed-pushforward stalk comparison and stalk exactness show both vanish outside i(W) and at xi, since the generic maps are isomorphisms. Each support is closed and contained in i(W) while omitting xi, hence strictly contained. Zero cokernels have empty support and satisfy the same conclusion.

theorem exists_integral_ideal_common_submodule (X W : Scheme.{u})
    [IsNoetherian X] (i : W ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsIntegral W]
    (G : X.Modules) (hGcoh : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace G)
    (hGsupp : {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (G.presheaf.stalk x)} = Set.range i.base)
    (hGann : ∀ a ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk (i.base (genericPoint W))),
      ∀ v : (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace
        (i.base (genericPoint W))).obj G, a • v = 0)
    (hGrank : ∃ inst : Module (X.residueField (i.base (genericPoint W)))
      ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace (i.base (genericPoint W))).obj G),
      (∀ (a : X.presheaf.stalk (i.base (genericPoint W)))
        (v : (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace
          (i.base (genericPoint W))).obj G),
        a • v = (X.residue (i.base (genericPoint W))) a • v) ∧
      Module.finrank (X.residueField (i.base (genericPoint W)))
        ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace (i.base (genericPoint W))).obj G)
        = 1)
    (I : W.IdealSheafData) (hI : ¬ IsZero ((pushforward i).obj I.toModules)) :
    ∃ (K : X.Modules) (a : K ⟶ G) (d : K ⟶ (pushforward i).obj I.toModules),
      Mono a ∧ Mono d ∧
      RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace (cokernel a) ∧
      RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace (cokernel d) ∧
      (cokernel a).IsFinitePresentation ∧ (cokernel d).IsFinitePresentation ∧
      {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton ((cokernel a).presheaf.stalk x)} ⊂ Set.range i.base ∧
      {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton ((cokernel d).presheaf.stalk x)} ⊂ Set.range i.base
